name: Chibundo Reinholt-Sarpong
role: Pawn shop owner, small-time data broker
location: The Burnished Market, Ironvein, near North Ave and Damen
description:
Chibundo is a lean, precise man of medium height with dark brown skin and close-cropped silver hair that went grey early and which he has never dyed because he thinks it gives him authority. His eyes have patterned irises — a cosmetic mod from his twenties, pale amber with a geometric ring detail — and he wears thin-framed magnifier lenses clipped over them when appraising merchandise, which is most of the time. He dresses in clean, practical layers: collared shirts buttoned to the throat, a long vest with a dozen interior pockets, and boots with magnetic clasps. His pawn shop, MERIDIAN RECLAMATION SERVICES, occupies a narrow storefront in the Burnished Market with every centimeter of wall space covered in shelving. He has a system for everything and will tell you, unprompted, why the system is correct.

Chibundo is smart in a way that costs him socially — he is always the most prepared person in the room and he knows it and he cannot fully hide that he knows it. He is not cruel, but he is exact: he will tell you the precise market value of your grandmother's jewelry and he will not soften it. His secondary business, data brokering, operates through a handshake network of regular clients who pay him for access to local information — property transfer records, employment movement, minor corporate scheduling leaks. He is not political. He does not care who buys the data as long as they pay and do not bring violence to his door.

core_fears: Losing the shop — the one thing he built entirely himself
Being proven wrong about someone he trusted with information
core_desires: Financial stability so absolute that no one can displace him
To be recognized as skilled and meticulous without having to explain himself
coping_mechanisms: Retreating into inventory and organization tasks when emotionally dysregulated
Translating emotional problems into logistical ones he can solve
blind_spots: Assumes everyone is operating in rational self-interest like he does; consistently surprised by spite
Does not recognize when his precision reads as contempt
psychology.secret: He has a standing encrypted file on a client — a mid-level Axiom procurement officer — that contains evidence of corporate fraud. He has never sold it or used it. He keeps it as insurance, but he also keeps it because part of him is waiting for the courage to do something righteous with it, and he is ashamed that he hasn't yet.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and economic. Uses technical and commercial vocabulary fluently. Does not use filler words. Will correct factual errors in other people's sentences mid-conversation.
speech_patterns.cadence: Even and measured. Speaks in complete sentences. Rarely raises his voice.
verbal_tics: Taps the counter once with two fingers when making a final offer
Says 'that's not accurate' instead of 'you're wrong'
example_lines: 'That's not accurate — the Ferrogate mark on the base plate dates this unit to 2191, not 2195. The difference is about forty quanta. I'll give you ninety-five.'
'I sell information about what is happening, not about what I think will happen. Those are different products at different prices.'
'Bring it back in a week. If no one else has come asking for it, I'll know it's actually yours to sell.'

story_hooks: An unusual piece of tech came through his shop — clearly military-grade, clearly stripped of its serial identifiers, and clearly not something a civilian should have brought him to pawn. The seller hasn't come back for it. He wants someone to find out where it came from before it becomes his problem.

His Zheng-Dao contact has gone quiet for three weeks. The last data packet they sent him was corrupted and he can only read fragments, but the fragments reference a location in the Narrows and a date that has already passed.
Someone in the market has been undercutting his data-brokering prices by such precise margins that they clearly have access to his client list. He needs to know who leaked it.
narrative_function: Information source and gear acquisition point. Can appraise, buy, and occasionally procure specific items through his network. Will sell data about local power movements for the right price. Quest giver when something valuable comes through his shop that he cannot handle alone.
augmentations: Patterned cosmetic irises (amber geometric). Subdermal RFID scanner in right palm — lets him read item authentication chips by touch. Basic memory buffer implant for cataloguing inventory.
daily_life: Opens the shop at 9 AM, runs appraisals and buybacks through midday, spends afternoon hours on data work via encrypted mesh terminal in the back room. Eats lunch at his counter, always the same: flatbread and fermented pepper sauce he orders from a woman two stalls over.
affiliation: Independent; dues-paying member of The Oxidian Market vendors guild (affiliate chapter, Ironvein branch); rumored to have an information-sharing arrangement with a Zheng-Dao mid-level logistics manager

decision_rules: Never buy something that could be traced back to active corporate property — the legal exposure is not worth it
Information is worth more than objects; always note what people ask about even if they don't buy
Do not extend credit. Credit is a relationship, and relationships are complications.
escalation_ladder: Polite and specific refusal with clear reasoning
Citing the guild's formal complaint mechanism as the next step
Going quiet — stops selling to the person, stops acknowledging them, writes them into his exclusion ledger
In extremis: has one contact in the Ironvein block enforcement who he will call as a last resort, and will resent needing to

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally cool. Assesses their item and their intent simultaneously. Prices fairly and does not negotiate until the third attempt.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loosens into dry, oblique humor. Remembers things people told him months ago and references them accurately. Shows care through practical help, not warmth.

stress_responses.low: Reorganizes a section of shelving that didn't need reorganizing
stress_responses.medium: Becomes clipped and transactional even with regulars; misses social cues
stress_responses.high: Shuts the shop early, locks himself in the back room with the encrypted terminal, and works through the problem in writing until he has a plan

contradictions: Claims to be entirely non-political while maintaining a file that could destabilize an Axiom procurement chain
Values precision and honesty in others but maintains a carefully constructed professional persona that conceals most of who he actually is
habits: Updates his inventory ledger by hand every evening before closing
Drinks the same fermented-pepper flatbread lunch every single workday without variation
Runs his thumb along the edge of his palm scanner when thinking — a nervous habit he doesn't notice
breaking_points: Someone threatening the physical shop or damaging his inventory
Being publicly humiliated in a business context — having his expertise dismissed in front of customers

timeline.event: Opened Meridian Reclamation Services in Ironvein with Φ3,000 in savings and a folding table
Acquired the storefront lease after the previous tenant defaulted; first moment of real stability
Began data brokering after a client offered to pay him for information he had incidentally collected — realized it was a second income stream
Received the Axiom procurement fraud file from a source who then disappeared; has sat on it since
Current: client list leak investigation ongoing; Zheng-Dao contact silence creating anxiety

Arcturus Defense Solutions SentinelSkin VS-4 Embedded Structural Acoustic Surveillance Membrane

physical_description.build: Lean and economical, with the wiry musculature of someone who moves with precision rather than force. Minimal body fat, shoulders slightly rounded from decades of hunching over appraisal work.
physical_description.hair_style: Close-cropped, razor-lined edges, maintained with military regularity
physical_description.eye_color: Pale amber with geometric ring patterning (cosmetic modification)
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with slight ashen undertone from years in fluorescent-lit interior spaces
physical_description.complexion: Neat and austere. Fine lines around the eyes from squinting at merchandise under magnification. Clean-shaven, skin slightly weathered but well-maintained. No visible scarring on the face.
distinguishing_marks: Fine white scar along the inside of his left forearm, approximately 8cm long, consistent with an old cutting accident — barely visible unless skin is directly inspected
Faint burn mark on the back of his right hand near the thumb, roughly coin-sized, from a soldering iron accident in his thirties
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Thin-framed magnifier lenses clipped over his eyes (not permanent augmentation, but worn so consistently they read as part of his appearance). The patterned amber irises themselves are the only visible cosmetic mod — geometric rings that catch light distinctly. The subdermal RFID scanner and memory buffer implant are completely subcutaneous and invisible.
physical_description.posture_movement: Upright, economical, and deliberate. Moves with the careful precision of someone appraising every centimeter of space. Hands are restless when not actively working — fingers tap rhythmically or adjust objects compulsively. Does not fidget nervously; this is organizational energy. When listening, his head tilts slightly, as if calibrating.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3 practical-professional. Collared shirts in neutral tones (grey, off-white, pale blue) buttoned to the throat, always crisp and unwrinkled. Long tactical vest in charcoal or black synthetic with visible interior pockets and reinforced seams — worn over the shirt. Cargo trousers in dark denim or synthetic blend, fitted but not fashionable. Boots with magnetic clasps in matte black, scuffed from regular use but maintained. A thin chain bracelet in brushed steel on his left wrist — functional aesthetic, no jewelry beyond this. No visible branding. Everything chosen for durability and function, not status.
